payload.alternatives: keep the Node supervisor without IPC (pipe still owned by Node); argv rendering in Rust (needs the ProviderAdapter binder; owner kept executor config as the argv source)
payload.rationale: The Node detached-run-supervisor held the agent's pipe and an IPC channel to the controller, so a dead controller (ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED) killed supervisor and agent and lost finished cli results (T8). Plan 6.2 built and proved the replacement: crash matrix through real bwrap and real fgos run, process-containment CI green on Linux, Windows and macOS, full suite green. Review threshold: an agent result lost after a controller or supervisor death, or a containment escape seen outside the named escapes.
payload.source: lane lead forgentx-95 under the owner's 2026-10-18 delegation; plan 6.2, design r6
payload.text: D-ADR0056: Run supervisor in Rust for the direct launch mode -- each attempt has one Rust supervisor (fgos internal supervise) and one launch gate (fgos internal gate) that roots the agent in a provably-empty containment domain (Linux: pid 1 of a PID namespace); the controller holds attempt.lock (+ cwd lease) before any side effect, writes an immutable digest-checked envelope v3, starts the supervisor detached with no pipe and no IPC, and from then only reads receipts from files; a dead supervisor leaves the agent running to exit or the gate's hard ceiling and the adopt door settles from gate-exit.json and the outbox; one door (sweepAttempts/adopt) for resume, recover, the run-start scan and doctor fix; attempt homes carry marker v2. Supersedes the detached-run-supervisor part of D-ADR0043; bound-invocation-supervisor stays.

payload.alternatives: keep the controller loop and harden the reaper (still loses the deadline when the controller dies); a second supervisor implementation for terminal mode (two doors for one attempt)
payload.rationale: The controller owned the herdr round loop (poll, deadline, settle, pane close): when it died all three were lost (T8 hB/hC/hD), and the reaper patch with pane ids in the home marker only treated the symptom and once nearly removed a live worker's home. Proven on real herdr: five CLIs settled pass, controller SIGKILL/SIGTERM and timeout rounds settle and keep or close the pane correctly, supervisor kill before and after the agent start ends as abandoned-not-started or orphan-result and adopt closes it.
payload.source: lane lead forgentx-95 under the owner's 2026-10-18 delegation; plan 6.3, design r6; docs/specs/runner.md
payload.text: D-ADR0059: The run supervisor watches herdr rounds through terminal-control, no longer the controller -- a herdr-spawn seat is a terminal-mode attempt of the one executeAssignment door (envelope v3 mode terminal, Rust supervisor and gate); the supervisor drives the pane through terminal-control by attempt id, the gate in the pane receives the attempt lock and cwd lease over SCM_RIGHTS, checks the peer uid and gives the agent the foreground tty; deadline, settle and pane close survive a dead controller (orphan-result, adopt, release-slot); release-slot closes the pane only on a clean end and otherwise keeps it; the attempt writer id is att-<attemptId> in both modes; the controller polling loop, herdr reconcile, liveness and the herdr part of the reaper are deleted

payload.alternatives: keep it as a lane note on the program board only (forgotten by the next audit); fold it into RUL11 (different concern: RUL11 gathers mess into one shape, this keeps the gathering from growing)
payload.rationale: Owner statement 2026-10-18 when assigning the low-level hardening lane: 'trong phạm vi code đang có ... tuyệt đối không mở rộng scope (scope creep), chỉ tốt hơn không bự hơn' and 'Chỉ thêm tính năng nếu nó thật sự đáng ... gom tất cả những ý tưởng cần thêm vào một chỗ ... giải thích rõ lý do và lợi ích'. It blocks an audit that answers a weakness by adding a flag, layer or mechanism, and feature ideas slipping into the fix list unchosen.
payload.source: owner, 2026-10-18 21:27 and 21:30; recorded by forgentx-95; docs/specs/platform-foundations.md RUL104
payload.text: D-ADR0061: RUL104 better, not bigger -- every audit, review or hardening of existing code makes what exists better (more stable, faster, lighter, simpler code; clearer, explicit, easier and more flexible APIs, signatures and contracts) within the existing scope and never bigger: no new feature, layer or mechanism; a changed contract moves every caller and deletes the old path in the same change (L10); a feature is added only when truly worth it: every feature idea goes into one separate section of the report with its reason (real problem, evidence) and benefit, and is built only after the owner chooses it

payload.alternatives: automatic resume after controller death (needs dead-controller detection and a single taker; deferred by name); resume that waits for a running attempt (--resume --wait, not built); relaunch on resume after gate-lost (would guess whether the agent ran)
payload.rationale: Controller death lost the attempt result (resume started over in runs/02), recover parked on result-N.json, and T8 left running attempts nobody cleaned. Proven by the crash matrix of r6 9.7 in direct and terminal mode, the resume and cancel tests, T8 rerun (8 cases incl. real herdr), and a full suite of 8190 tests on the integration tip.
payload.source: lane lead forgentx-95 under the owner's 2026-10-18 delegation; plan 6.4, design r6 §16; docs/specs/runner.md
payload.text: D-ADR0060: A dead controller leaves a settled attempt and a unit awaiting an explicit --resume; automatic resume is a named deferral -- Ctrl-C/SIGTERM of fgos run asks the supervisor to cancel the delivered attempt, waits dispatch.cancelWaitMs for its receipt and exits 130/143; --resume asks adopt first: a closed attempt with a result is used as is and the agent never runs again, after a cancelled or abandoned attempt the unit runs again in a new attempt that points back to it, a running or legacy attempt is refused by name, a second concurrent resume is refused resume-in-progress, and a bound attempt is never given a second supervisor; recover gains adopt and abandon-legacy; runs from before the supervisor stuck running are settled abandoned-legacy by doctor only when every recorded pid is dead; binding present with a dead gate stays gate-lost (fail closed)

payload.alternatives: DAG runner with a prose conductor; CMMN sentry/expression engine; Work lifecycle FSM as engine; full CMMN engine; admission inside Execution Core; loosening the A4 architecture guard; admission in Rust now; Event Store with advance re-rank now; N17 shape A or B; host relay for confined nested writes
payload.rationale: 0049 ended authority sprawl but also took ordering judgement from the agent, against the hard-outside soft-inside vision and the owner direction of 2026-10-18; 0 of 89 stored runs were coding/feature; lead chain 6.4 slipped prose-only rules three times while machine guards held. Flexibility goes to the agent, constraints to machine guards: closed catalog of six MUST checks, N1 fail-closed authority on writing dispatch into a case-bound worktree, AdmissionPort owned by Execution Core and implemented by Workflow, Shape C for advance, JSONL ledger hardened in place. Owner 2026-10-19: 08:46 N1; 12:20 Shape C, Playbook proposer, refuse confined nested writes, N1 limited to the two doors, no Event Store; 12:32 spec approved; 12:35 feature ideas F1-F7, F9, F11, F12.
payload.text: D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger): a Workflow is an operating guide plus constraints, not a script. The agent proposes the order; the Workflow case admits each activity against its ledger and records progress. Narrows 0048 §2 (agent proposes, case admits and records) and 0049 §4 (Workflow is the single authority for admission and the progress record, not the chooser of order); 0048 §1, §3, §4 and 0049 §1-3 stay.
